passages.text: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God asks if Job knows when mountain goats give birth.
God asks if Job has watched the doe bear her fawn.
passages.original: הֲיָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֭ת לֶ֣דֶת יַעֲלֵי־ סָ֑לַע חֹלֵ֖ל אַיָּל֣וֹת תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃

passages.text: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about animals.
God refers to mountain goats and deer.
God says, "Can you count the months they are pregnant?"
God asks, "Do you know the time they give birth?"
passages.original: תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה׃

passages.text: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
passages.sermon:
Mountain goats crouch down.
They give birth to their young.
They deliver their newborn.
passages.original: תִּ֭כְרַעְנָה יַלְדֵיהֶ֣ן תְּפַלַּ֑חְנָה חֶבְלֵיהֶ֥ם תְּשַׁלַּֽחְנָה׃

passages.text: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
passages.sermon:
The young ones of wild animals live in the open field.
They grow strong there.
They leave their mothers.
They do not come back.
passages.original: יַחְלְמ֣וּ בְ֭נֵיהֶם יִרְבּ֣וּ בַבָּ֑ר יָ֝צְא֗וּ וְלֹא־ שָׁ֥בוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
passages.sermon:
God created the wild donkey.
God set the wild donkey free.
God released the swift donkey from its harness.
No human did this.
Only God gave the wild donkey its freedom.
passages.original: מִֽי־ שִׁלַּ֣ח פֶּ֣רֶא חָפְשִׁ֑י וּמֹסְר֥וֹת עָ֝ר֗וֹד מִ֣י פִתֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the wild donkey.
God says, "I made the wilderness his home."
God says, "I made the salt flats his dwelling."
God chose these places for the wild donkey to live.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֣מְתִּי עֲרָבָ֣ה בֵית֑וֹ וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֥יו מְלֵֽחָה׃

passages.text: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
passages.sermon:
The wild donkey scorns the noise of the city.
He does not care about the busy crowds.
He never hears the shouts of a driver.
He ignores the commands of people.
passages.original: יִ֭שְׂחַק לַהֲמ֣וֹן קִרְיָ֑ה תְּשֻׁא֥וֹת נ֝וֹגֵ֗שׂ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
passages.sermon:
God made the wild donkey live in the wilderness.
The wild donkey does not live in the city.
The wild donkey roams the mountains.
He looks for pasture in the mountains.
He searches for any green plant to eat.
passages.original: יְת֣וּר הָרִ֣ים מִרְעֵ֑הוּ וְאַחַ֖ר כָּל־ יָר֣וֹק יִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
passages.sermon:
The wild ox is a strong and untamed animal.
He does not agree to serve you.
He will not stay by your manger at night.
You cannot make the wild ox your servant.
You cannot keep him close like a tame animal.
passages.original: הֲיֹ֣אבֶה רֵּ֣ים עָבְדֶ֑ךָ אִם־ יָ֝לִ֗ין עַל־ אֲבוּסֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
passages.sermon:
The wild ox is strong and untamed.
You cannot control him with a harness.
You cannot make him walk straight in the furrow.
He will not plow the valleys behind you.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽתִקְשָׁר־ רֵ֭ים בְּתֶ֣לֶם עֲבֹת֑וֹ אִם־ יְשַׂדֵּ֖ד עֲמָקִ֣ים אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
passages.sermon:
The wild ox is very strong.
You see his great strength.
Can you trust him because he is strong?
Will you give your hard work to him?
Will you depend on him to finish your work?
passages.original: הֲֽתִבְטַח־ בּ֭וֹ כִּי־ רַ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ וְתַעֲזֹ֖ב אֵלָ֣יו יְגִיעֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the wild ox.
The wild ox is very strong.
God asks if you can trust the wild ox.
Can you trust the wild ox to return with your grain?
Can you trust the wild ox to gather your harvest to your threshing floor?
passages.original: הֲתַאֲמִ֣ין בּ֭וֹ כִּי־ יָשׁוּב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְֽגָרְנְךָ֥ יֶאֱסֹֽף׃

passages.text: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
passages.sermon:
The ostrich has wings.
The ostrich flaps its wings with joy.
The ostrich’s wings cannot compare to the wings and feathers of the stork.
The stork has strong pinions and fine feathers.
The ostrich’s wings are not like the stork’s wings.
passages.original: כְּנַף־ רְנָנִ֥ים נֶעֱלָ֑סָה אִם־ אֶ֝בְרָ֗ה חֲסִידָ֥ה וְנֹצָֽה׃

passages.text: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
passages.sermon:
The ostrich is a large bird.
She lays her eggs on the ground.
She leaves her eggs there.
She lets the eggs warm in the sand.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תַעֲזֹ֣ב לָאָ֣רֶץ בֵּצֶ֑יהָ וְֽעַל־ עָפָ֥ר תְּחַמֵּֽם׃

passages.text: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
passages.sermon:
The ostrich is a large bird.
The ostrich lays its eggs on the ground.
The ostrich forgets about its eggs.
A person might step on the eggs.
A wild animal might trample the eggs.
passages.original: וַ֭תִּשְׁכַּח כִּי־ רֶ֣גֶל תְּזוּרֶ֑הָ וְחַיַּ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה תְּדוּשֶֽׁהָ׃

passages.text: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
passages.sermon:
The ostrich is a bird.
She treats her young harshly.
She acts as if her young do not belong to her.
She does not care that her work may be wasted.
She shows no fear or concern for her effort.
passages.original: הִקְשִׁ֣יחַ בָּנֶ֣יהָ לְּלֹא־ לָ֑הּ לְרִ֖יק יְגִיעָ֣הּ בְּלִי־ פָֽחַד׃

passages.text: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
passages.sermon: God made her without wisdom.\r\nGod did not give her understanding.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ חָכְמָ֑ה וְלֹא־ חָ֥לַק לָ֝֗הּ בַּבִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
passages.sermon:
The ostrich is a large bird.
She cannot fly.
She spreads her wings high in the air.
She does this with pride.
She sees the horse and its rider.
She laughs at them.
She does not fear them.
passages.original: כָּ֭עֵת בַּמָּר֣וֹם תַּמְרִ֑יא תִּֽשְׂחַ֥ק לַ֝סּ֗וּס וּלְרֹֽכְבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God says, "Do you give the horse its strength?"
God says, "Do you clothe the horse’s neck with a flowing mane?"
passages.original: הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God describes the horse.
God asks Job a question.
God says, "Do you make the horse leap like a locust?"
The horse leaps with great energy.
The horse's proud snorting causes terror.
passages.original: הְֽ֭תַרְעִישֶׁנּוּ כָּאַרְבֶּ֑ה ה֖וֹד נַחְר֣וֹ אֵימָֽה׃

passages.text: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
passages.sermon:
The horse is strong and brave.
He paws the ground in the valley.
He feels joy in his strength.
He runs forward to meet weapons in battle.
passages.original: יַחְפְּר֣וּ בָ֭עֵמֶק וְיָשִׂ֣ישׂ בְּכֹ֑חַ יֵ֝צֵ֗א לִקְרַאת־ נָֽשֶׁק׃

passages.text: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a warhorse.
The warhorse feels no fear.
The warhorse laughs at danger.
Nothing frightens the warhorse.
The warhorse does not run from the sword.
The warhorse stands firm in battle.
passages.original: יִשְׂחַ֣ק לְ֭פַחַד וְלֹ֣א יֵחָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־ יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
passages.sermon:
The horse stands ready for battle.
A quiver rattles at the horse’s side.
A flashing spear is near the horse.
A lance is also near the horse.
passages.original: עָ֭לָיו תִּרְנֶ֣ה אַשְׁפָּ֑ה לַ֖הַב חֲנִ֣ית וְכִידֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
passages.sermon:
The subject is a warhorse.
The warhorse trembles with excitement.
The warhorse moves quickly across the land.
He covers great distances.
He cannot stand still when he hears the sound of the ram’s horn.
The sound of the horn signals battle.
The warhorse eagerly responds to this sound.
passages.original: בְּרַ֣עַשׁ וְ֭רֹגֶז יְגַמֶּא־ אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹֽא־ יַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּי־ ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃

passages.text: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar— the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
passages.sermon:
The warhorse hears the blast of the horn.
He snorts with excitement.
He smells the battle from far away.
He hears the shouts of commanders.
He hears the cry of war.
passages.original: בְּדֵ֤י שֹׁפָ֨ר׀ יֹ֘אמַ֤ר הֶאָ֗ח וּֽ֭מֵרָחוֹק יָרִ֣יחַ מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥עַם שָׂ֝רִים וּתְרוּעָֽה׃

passages.text: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
passages.sermon:
The hawk is a bird.
The hawk flies.
The hawk spreads his wings.
The hawk flies toward the south.
You do not give the hawk understanding.
The hawk does not fly because of your wisdom.
The hawk does not spread his wings because you command him.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַֽאֲבֶר־ נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ כְּנָפוֹ לְתֵימָֽן׃

passages.text: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks about the eagle.
God says, “Does the eagle soar because you command him?”
God says, “Does the eagle build his nest high because you tell him to?”
passages.original: אִם־ עַל־ פִּ֭יךָ יַגְבִּ֣יהַּ נָ֑שֶׁר וְ֝כִ֗י יָרִ֥ים קִנּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
passages.sermon:
The eagle is a large, powerful bird.
\r\nThe eagle lives on a cliff.
\r\nThe eagle stays there.
\r\nThe eagle makes his stronghold on a rocky crag.
passages.original: סֶ֣לַע יִ֭שְׁכֹּן וְיִתְלֹנָ֑ן עַֽל־ שֶׁן־ סֶ֝֗לַע וּמְצוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
passages.sermon: The eagle lives on a high cliff.\r\nHe looks for food from that place.\r\nHis eyes see food far away.
passages.original: מִשָּׁ֥ם חָֽפַר־ אֹ֑כֶל לְ֝מֵרָח֗וֹק עֵינָ֥יו יַבִּֽיטוּ׃

passages.text: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
passages.sermon:
The eagle is a bird of prey.
\r\nThe eagle has young ones.
\r\nThe young ones eat blood.
\r\nThe eagle goes where there are dead bodies.
\r\nThe eagle is present where the slain are.
passages.original: וְאֶפְרֹחוֹ יְעַלְעוּ־ דָ֑ם וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חֲ֝לָלִ֗ים שָׁ֣ם הֽוּא׃פ
